summary: Kootenai County Copper Mountain: tree platform c.1918, 40-ft pole tower 1923, 50-ft steel tower 1940, moved to Faset Peak 1954; now gone.

facts.design: 40-foot pole tower with 6x6 cab (1923), later a 50-foot steel tower; L-4 ground cabin added 1934
facts.status_note: The L-4 cab was removed in 1950 and the steel tower moved to Faset Peak in 1954. Idaho Fire Lookouts lists the lookout as removed. Footings remain at the summit per Willhite.

access.note: Hike-in on Coeur d'Alene National Forest land. The level is inferred from the hike route and national forest ownership; no source states an access rule. Willhite describes a gated road that is walked or biked.

visit.trail_note: Willhite: about 2 miles one way from Marie Saddle, 900 ft gain. Alternatively, park on a saddle on FR 3907 and walk or bike the gated road to the summit.

corrections.proposed: 40-foot pole tower with 6x6 cab (1923); L-4 cab added on the ground for living quarters in 1934
corrections.why: The L-4 cab was a ground living cabin added in 1934, not the lookout cab. The lookout cab sat on a 40-foot pole tower and later on a 50-foot steel tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts and Willhite give 1940. The Weebly list gives 1942. The story gives 1940 and notes the 1942 date.
Firelookout.com's heading gives R.I.P. 1923-1942, but the same page gives a steel tower move in 1954 and an L-4 removal in 1950. The later dates are used.
Willhite's survey notes place the steel tower at the lower point, while an image looks like the high point and the newest footings are at the high point. The story says the exact spot is uncertain.
Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 5007 ft. Willhite gives 5,012 ft for the summit. The story does not use the elevation.

notes_for_editor: Four pages with a clear build sequence, but they disagree on the steel tower year (1940 vs 1942), and firelookout.com's R.I.P. span does not match its own later entries. The record's height_m 12.2 (40 ft) matches the 1923 pole tower, not the later 50-foot steel tower (about 15.2 m), so it was left as is. The design correction is in corrections. Staffing is one named lookout (1944), and the name is not used in the story. The story says footings remain at the summit only as Willhite describes them. The access 'public' level is inferred. The index lists the Boundary and Kootenai Copper Mountains separately, which the story notes so readers do not confuse them.
